newsitem.title: VIETNAM: New Vietnam-China train service planned.
newsitem.headline: New Vietnam-China train service planned.

text.p: Vietnam said on Friday it was hoping to resume passenger traffic on a meandering colonial rail line heading northwest from Hanoi across a remote mountainous border region to the Chinese city of Kunming.

At present, the line is used for occasional local passenger trains and freight, but a railway official said agreement at the provincial level had now been reached for a three-car international passenger service.
"We're just waiting for the ministerial level go-ahead," he said. "We're expecting this soon."
Rail links between Vietnam and China were restored earlier this year, 17 years after they were severed by a border war.

But traffic on the Hanoi-Kunming line has been freight only so far. Passengers must take local trains, walk across a bridge at the border crossing, and then catch another train to reach destinations in China.

The official said the new service would see international passenger cars attached to a train from Hanoi, shunted across the border and then coupled to another train bound for the capital of Southern Yunnan province.
Expected travel time is about 31 hours.
